claims.text: Conventional SPS-fabricated W–Cu composites have a random microstructure with isolated phases.
Directional SPS using a controlled temperature gradient and uniaxial pressure will produce continuous, aligned nanoscale Cu layers interleaved with W lamellae.
Directional SPS will create a percolating Cu network oriented along the primary thermal-transport axis.
Directional SPS will form coherent, defect-minimized W/Cu interfaces.
A processing temperature of 1000–1200 °C under a controlled temperature gradient and uniaxial loading is suitable for producing the proposed W–Cu architecture.
Aligned Cu layers provide continuous thermal-transport pathways.
The aligned Cu pathways reduce interfacial phonon scattering.
The aligned Cu pathways reduce interfacial electron scattering.
Reduced phonon and electron interfacial scattering increases the composite's effective thermal conductivity.
Coherent interfaces can improve interfacial adhesion and thereby contribute to mechanical integrity.
The W lamellae will maintain the mechanical integrity of the directionally processed composite.
The W lamellae will retain irradiation resistance in the directionally processed composite.
The directional SPS-processed W–Cu composite will have at least 20% higher axial thermal conductivity than an otherwise comparable randomly structured SPS composite.
The thermal-conductivity increase will occur without loss of mechanical strength.
The thermal-conductivity increase will occur without loss of irradiation resistance.
The predicted performance will hold under high thermal flux and irradiation conditions typical of fusion-reactor joints.
Directional structuring may produce anisotropic mechanical performance under multiaxial loading.
